question: An asset that the borrower owns and uses this as a guarantee to a lender until the loan is repaid is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Collateral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Collateral** is an asset that a borrower offers to a lender as security for a loan.
 
• If the borrower defaults on the loan, the lender has the right to seize the collateral to recover the loan amount.
 
• Collateral helps reduce the risk for the lender, making it easier for borrowers to get loans.
 
• Common forms of collateral include real estate, vehicles, and equipment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interest**

 
 
• Interest is the cost of borrowing money, typically expressed as an annual percentage of the loan amount.
 
• It is the amount a lender charges for the use of their money or the amount earned on an investment.
 
 
 
• **Credit**
 
 
• Credit is the ability to borrow money or access goods or services with the understanding that you will pay later.
 
• It is often measured by a credit score, which helps lenders evaluate the creditworthiness of a borrower.
 
 
 
• **Debit**
 
 
• Debit refers to a deduction from a bank account balance, typically due to a transaction or withdrawal.
 
• In accounting, it is an entry on the left side of a ledger, representing an increase in assets or a decrease in liabilities.
